title: Observable Cut Descriptions of Sharp Quantile-Panel Identified Sets under Predeterminedness
banked_reason: Cold tier review: tier incremental, paper-score ceiling 6.3 below field floor 7.4, salvageable false, with no bounded fix in scope; math review passed.
gap_reasons: The recorded proposal selected feedback-compatible residual-collision identification conditions and an adapted observable dual as principal deliverables, but this core instead makes a different representability-recognition problem open.

The advertised direct-observable frontier is not characterized: the facet/rank theorem tests a polytope only after its facets and rank oracle are known, while polynomial recognition on the signed prefix structure remains the open question prefix-cut-frontier.

The obstruction families establish linear facet proliferation and failure of ordinary subset cuts, but they do not supply general slope-identification conditions, complexity bounds, inference, or evidence that the proposed geometry materially improves applied panel analysis.
proof_attempt_summary: Two proposal angles and four D0 solve rounds established a sound finite-prefix compatibility LP, exact binary recovery, and minimal T=2 and stronger T=3 complete-path obstruction families. The promised adapted-dual and residual-collision package did not survive as the principal result, and the signed-incidence recognition theorem remained open; independent review therefore capped the package at incremental tier despite a clean mathematics review.
tldr: The note asks when sharp fixed-\(T\) quantile-panel identification under genuine predeterminedness admits a direct observable cut description rather than only a latent residual-anchor LP. It proves the finite prefix reduction, augmented selectionability specialization, exact facet/rank test, and binary weighted separation. The corrected family \(\mathcal E_m\) is binary residual and establishes all three minimal elbows: at \(T=2\), three atoms per stratum, and \(J(0)=2\), both prefix and complete-path median models give \(\mathcal P_0=\{q:q_{g3}\le q_{g1}\}\), with \(F(0)=m\) and a three-level facet normal; with one anchor, \(\mathcal P_b=\Delta_L\). The two retained \(T=3\), three-anchor families give the stronger \(F(0)=4m\) growth. Polynomial recognition on the signed labeled structure remains open.
gap: The complete-path model has sharp coupling and computation, and generic selection theory can profile latent effects, but neither result identifies when the weaker prefix-conditioned model has a concise direct observable description. Ordinary core-determining classes use subset-capacity facets; exact three-level enumeration shows that the prefix projection can have genuinely weighted facet normals outside that geometry.
fill: The work will prove the finite prefix reduction, derive the augmented selectionability specialization, establish the facet/rank equivalence, and characterize observable residual-order incidence patterns that pass it. The explicit five-type family gives a reproducible failure mode and a linear exact facet benchmark, so a negative result remains substantive.
